newsitem.title: USA: A.M. Best downgrades Prudential property unit.
newsitem.headline: A.M. Best downgrades Prudential property unit.

text.p: Insurance rating agency A.M. Best Monday lowered the claims-paying ability rating of Prudential Insurance Co. of America's main property-casualty unit, citing its poor operating earnings, earnings volatility and above-average catastrophe risk.
The downgrade, to B++ from A-, applies to Prudential Property and Casualty Insurance Co. and its three reinsured affiliates, which have suffered major pretax operating losses over the past six years.

The group's poor 1996 operating results and financial projections for the next several years led the insurance rating agency to lower its ratings, which measure the risk that consumers' insurance claims will not be paid.
Prudential said it was disappointed and disagreed with Best's action.
"We believe that PRUPAC's operating results and its track record don't warrant the action taken by Best," a Prudential spokesman said.
The ratings indicate the financial strength of the insurer, and insurers often have a harder time attracting business with less than an A rating.
However, the new rating still falls within A.M. Best's "secure" range, reflecting the backing of the group's parent company.
Prudential showed its strong support with its $725 million capital infusion into the property/casualty unit in 1992 to offset huge losses from Hurricane Andrew in that year.

The rating also reflects the group's much-improved balance sheet strength and risk profile, reduced underwriting leverage, and substantial catastrophe mitigation progress in Florida, California and the Northeast, A.M. Best said.
A.M. Best also said it was encouraged by Prudential's commitment to the group's new management team, which plans a number of marketing, distribution and operational initiatives.

A.M. Best said it did not expect the group to report meaningful positive returns until 1998, largely due to larger losses than its national peers as well as expenses stemming from systems investments and constraints on premium growth due to tighter underwriting standards.

A.M. Best said it was encouraged that the group's most recent initiatives begun in spring under current management have shown early signs of improved business within its downsized personal insurance lines.

Those initiatives will bring much greater underwriting discipline and market focus to the property/casualty unit, and are necessary for the group to become a profitable, self-sufficient unit, A.M. Best said.
